content.quote_text: These sources collectively explore the complex and unresolved concept of intelligence, contrasting perspectives from artificial intelligence (AI) and cognitive psychology. One central theme is the debate around representation in AI systems, with Brooks arguing that explicit world models can hinder simple intelligence and that the abstraction of perception is the hard problem often performed by researchers, not the AI itself. Simultaneously, other authors like Chollet, Da Silveira and Lopes, and the psychometric texts, focus on defining and measuring general human intelligence, often emphasizing skill-acquisition efficiency and the importance of innate cognitive priors like Core Knowledge for fair benchmarking. The discussion is framed by foundational philosophical challenges to AI, such as Searle's Chinese Room argument, which questions whether machines manipulating formal symbols can genuinely possess understanding or intentionality.

content.quote_text:
In Freud and Philosophy (1965), Paul Ricoeur coins "hermeneutics of suspicion" for readers who treat meanings as disguises to be unmasked. His "masters of suspicion" are Marx, Nietzsche, Freud:
• Marx: surface meanings = ideology; decode them into class interest.
• Freud: manifest content = symptom; interpret toward latent desire/repression.
• Nietzsche: moral claims = sublimated drives; genealogy exposes resentment and will-to-power.

content.quote_text: Erroneous conversion of gene names into other data types has been a frustration for computational biologists for years. We hypothesized that such errors in supplementary files might diminish after a report in 2016 highlighting the extent of the problem. To assess this, we performed a scan of supplementary files published in PubMed Central from 2014 to 2020. Overall, gene name errors continued to accumulate unabated in the period after 2016. An improved scanning software we developed identified gene name errors in 30.9% (3,436/11,117) of articles with supplementary Excel gene lists; a figure significantly higher than previously estimated. This is due to gene names being converted not just to dates and floating-point numbers, but also to internal date format (five-digit numbers). These findings further reinforce that spreadsheets are ill-suited to use with large genomic data.

content.quote_text: Large language models (LLMs) excel at few-shot in-context learning (ICL) – learning from a few examples provided in context at inference, without any weight updates. Newly expanded context windows allow us to investigate ICL with hundreds or thousands of examples –the many-shot regime. Going from few-shot to many-shot, we observe significant performance gains across a wide variety of generative and discriminative tasks. While promising, many-shot ICL can be bottlenecked by the available amount of human-generated outputs. To mitigate this limitation, we explore two new settings: “Reinforced ICL” and “Unsupervised ICL”. Reinforced ICL uses model-generated chain-of-thought rationales in place of human rationales. Unsupervised ICL removes rationales from the prompt altogether and prompts the model only with

content.quote_text: These sources collectively discuss the concept of schemas and frames as fundamental cognitive structures for processing information, understanding language, and guiding behavior. They explore how these mental frameworks, whether unconscious or actively constructed, allow individuals to interpret sensory data, retrieve memories, and make sense of the world, often by integrating new experiences with existing knowledge. The texts also highlight the distinction between tacit knowing (knowing how) and explicit knowledge (knowing that), suggesting that much of human understanding and skill operates through unarticulated, schema-driven processes. Furthermore, the sources examine the role of these cognitive structures in areas like pattern recognition, memory recall, and speech perception, while also considering their implications for artificial intelligence and the design of intelligent systems.

The image displays a presentation slide with a white background and black text. It is titled 'Slide 9: Jagged Frontier of AI Capabilities' and includes two bullet points. The first bullet point describes a graph titled 'Jagged Frontier of AI Capabilities' showing a wavy blue line for actual abilities and a smooth dashed line for expectations. The second bullet point provides a verbatim transcript of a speaker's commentary on the concept.
content.quote_text: "And, uh, the first thing that's important to know when you first start using, um, anything based on this new generation of AI, based on large language models, is the jagged frontier, which is where we have a distinction between what our frontier of expectations, uh, that the large language models, um, can do. And unfortunately, uh, what impression people form about what models can do very often is quite by the accident of what they first ask the model to do. So, if you ask about something that you would not expect an AI tool to be able to do, you may walk away with an, uh, impression that ChatGPT is the best thing ever and there's really literally nothing it cannot do. Whereas if you ask something that is very similar to it, uh, or at least seemingly similar to you, uh, but um, and ChatGPT cannot do it, well, it feels like it is useless. And so, for example, one good example is that it can count themes and stories in a, in a, uh, paragraph, but it cannot, uh, count words, uh, but bad at, uh, finding ideas, but with large language models and AI of the new generation, it's exactly the opposite."

content.quote_text: The move from a structuralist account in which capital is understood to structure social relations in relatively homologous ways to a view of hegemony in which power relations are subject to repetition, convergence, and rearticulation brought the question of temporality into the thinking of structure, and marked a shift from a form of Althusserian theory that takes structural totalities as theoretical objects to one in which the insights into the contingent possibility of structure inaugurate a renewed conception of hegemony as bound up with the contingent sites and strategies of the rearticulation of power.
